Coin Metrics: Meme Coins Hit All-Time Highs in 17.2 Days on Average, Only 3% Recover According to Bloomberg, a Coin Metrics report shows that meme coins reach all-time highs an average of 17.2 days after their first trade, with one-quarter peaking within 1.6 days. The median time from peak to a 95% decline into a “dead” state is 370 days, and only 3% of meme coins return to their all-time highs. — link

Strive Upsizes SATS Preferred IPO to 7 Million Shares, Raising About $630 Million Strive has upsized its 15% Series A Perpetual SATS Preferred Stock IPO by 2 million shares to 7 million shares, priced at $90 per share. Gross proceeds are expected to be about $630 million before underwriting discounts, commissions and offering expenses. Settlement is scheduled for October 20. Proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, including bitcoin and bitcoin-related products, working capital, income-generating assets, capital expenditures, share repurchases and potential acquisitions. — link

Highlight Clip: Arthur Hayes: Trading Other Assets to Buy More Bitcoin Arthur Hayes: Trading Other Assets to Buy More Bitcoin On October 13, 2026, Maelstrom co-founder Arthur Hayes said in an interview with The Rollup that whether scarce assets like Bitcoin or on-chain businesses outperform depends on the entry price, market capitalization, and the protocol and smart contract risks investors are willing to take. He suggested that a token with a market cap below 1 billion could outperform Bitcoin if demand from AI agents drives a valuation re-rating. Discussing his own allocation, Hayes said the fund’s Bitcoin position is so large that its other holdings are insignificant by comparison. Even when the fund holds substantial positions in ETH or other tokens, it takes profits and uses them to buy more Bitcoin. Trading other assets to generate profits and accumulate more Bitcoin is the fund’s core objective. WuBlockchain notes that Arthur Hayes' market forecasts have had a low historical accuracy rate and that his views frequently change. Readers are advised to focus on his analytical framework rather than specific price targets or timing predictions. — link

OKX CMO Haider Rafique Plans to Leave by End of 2026 OKX Global Managing Partner and CMO Haider Rafique plans to leave by the end of 2026, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Rafique joined OKX in March 2020, led the exchange’s rebranding, and drove partnerships including with the McLaren F1 team and the Tribeca Film Festival. He also helped facilitate Intercontinental Exchange’s $200 million strategic investment in OKX in March, which valued the exchange at $25 billion. Both OKX and Rafique declined to comment. — link
